name: Manufacturing
metaDescription: Explore manufacturing HR with Hirebrew: site hiring, structured interviews, onboarding ownership and employee support across plants and offices.
headline: Keep people moving. Across every site.
subhead: Connect plant managers, central HR and employees through clearer hiring, onboarding and everyday people support.
summary: Connect site hiring, local onboarding and employee support across your operation.
challengeTitle: Production has a plan. People handoffs need one too.
challenge: A replacement request starts at a plant. Approval happens at head office. Interviews involve a technical supervisor, while a different team prepares the new starter. When each handoff lives in its own conversation, nobody sees the whole journey. Hirebrew brings these people workflows into one product direction, with named responsibilities from requisition to the first manager check-in.

priorities.title: Make site demand visible
priorities.body: Capture the role, location and hiring rationale before recruitment begins. Give site leaders and HR a shared starting point for discussing vacancies instead of reconciling separate lists at the end of the week.

priorities.title: Keep technical hiring structured
priorities.body: Bring supervisors into interview panels and use scorecards to record role-relevant evidence. Keep candidate questions in the hiring conversation so practical details do not disappear between central recruitment and the site.

priorities.title: Carry ownership past the offer
priorities.body: Assign onboarding tasks to the people who can complete them. Follow the welcome with employee requests, learning conversations and manager check-ins, connecting plant and office employees to the same people-service approach.

workflowTitle: From a site vacancy to a supported starter.
workflowIntro: A proposed pilot for one plant and one job family. Use sample records to test where central and local responsibilities meet.

steps.label: Request
steps.title: Describe the vacancy
steps.body: Raise a requisition with the location and role requirements. Route the request through the agreed approval path before HR opens the candidate pipeline.

steps.label: Select
steps.title: Compare the evidence
steps.body: Coordinate candidate stages, panel participation and structured feedback. Use two-way messaging to resolve candidate questions before the next step.

steps.label: Prepare
steps.title: Assign the first-week tasks
steps.body: Make the welcome, introductions and local onboarding responsibilities visible. Keep specialist safety sign-off with the qualified team and its established system.

steps.label: Support
steps.title: Keep the conversation going
steps.body: Explore leave, letters and employee requests alongside development goals. Use early check-ins to identify where a new colleague still needs support.

capabilities.name: Requisition approvals
capabilities.body: Give each site's hiring need a clear starting point and decision owner.

capabilities.name: Panels and scorecards
capabilities.body: Bring role-specific interview evidence into a shared hiring discussion.

capabilities.name: Onboarding tasks
capabilities.body: Coordinate the people responsible for the first week and early check-ins.

capabilities.name: Workforce views
capabilities.body: Explore the headcount and department context needed for planning conversations.

ai.title: A clearer first-week brief.
ai.body: Brew AI concepts can help draft a role-specific onboarding outline from approved requirements. A site leader reviews the language, responsibilities and omissions. The website demonstrates illustrative drafting, not live safety guidance or automated decisions.
ai.example: Draft a first-week welcome plan for a maintenance technician. Include manager introductions and learning discussions. Leave safety authorisation to the site's approved process.

pilot.title: Start with one plant, not your whole operation.
pilot.body: Walk through a sample vacancy with a supervisor, recruiter and employee representative. Agree what successful ownership looks like before expanding to other sites.
checks: Test frontline access and mobile usability on the devices people actually use.

pilot.boundary: This preview does not provide shift rostering, time-and-attendance, safety certification or payroll execution. Production access controls and integrations require validation.

faqs.q: Can we use different onboarding tasks by site?
faqs.a: Location-specific responsibilities are a useful pilot scenario for Hirebrew's task-based onboarding. Test the setup with your actual operating model before making a multi-site rollout commitment.

faqs.q: Does Hirebrew replace our plant systems?
faqs.a: No. The focus is hiring and employee coordination. Production planning, clocking, shift scheduling and safety systems remain specialist tools; any required connection must be scoped separately.

faqs.q: What should a Nigerian manufacturing pilot include?
faqs.a: Include both frontline and office participants, realistic connectivity conditions and the languages used for employee support. Validate those access needs rather than assuming a desktop-first process will suit every site.

priorities.body: Agree the role before hiring, involve the right interviewers and record role-relevant scorecards. Give candidates a two-way communication route while keeping the panel accountable for evidence and the final decision.

priorities.title: Make onboarding a team responsibility
priorities.body: Assign introductions, first-week tasks and early manager check-ins. Clarify the handoff to IT and other owners without pretending a people task automatically provisions accounts or grants production access.

priorities.title: Connect growth to regular conversations
priorities.body: Explore goals, feedback, learning and development needs as teams evolve. Give managers a repeatable structure while leaving room for the differences between engineering, product, design and commercial roles.

workflowTitle: From an approved role to a confident start.
workflowIntro: A proposed pilot around one product team. Use sample records to connect its hiring manager, interview panel, HR and onboarding owners.

steps.label: Define
steps.title: Agree what the team needs
steps.body: Raise a requisition and clarify role expectations. Establish the approval path and evidence the interview panel should look for.

steps.label: Interview
steps.title: Make the decision discussable
steps.body: Coordinate panel participation, candidate stages and structured feedback. Keep candidate questions connected to the process rather than leaving them in a separate thread.

steps.label: Onboard
steps.title: Join up the first weeks
steps.body: Assign introductions, learning tasks and 30/60/90-day check-ins. Keep account provisioning and specialist access approvals in the systems that own them.

steps.label: Grow
steps.title: Turn expectations into conversations
steps.body: Explore goals, feedback and learning needs. Use the early check-ins to discuss context and support, not to replace professional judgement with an automated score.

capabilities.name: Candidate pipeline and messaging
capabilities.body: Keep the hiring journey visible and give candidates a way to reply.

capabilities.name: Structured interview panels
capabilities.body: Bring technical and cross-functional perspectives into shared scorecards.

capabilities.name: 30/60/90-day onboarding
capabilities.body: Explore a deliberate transition from new starter to supported team member.

capabilities.name: Goals, feedback and learning
capabilities.body: Connect development discussions with the employee's role and manager.

ai.title: Useful drafting, with the manager in control.
ai.body: Brew AI's illustrative drafts can help structure an interview guide, onboarding outline or check-in agenda using approved role information. A person reviews the result. The website does not run live model inference or automatically rank applicants.
ai.example: Draft an onboarding outline for a product engineer. Include introductions, learning goals and manager check-ins. Do not invent access rights, delivery deadlines or performance expectations.

pilot.title: Pilot with one cross-functional team.
pilot.body: Choose a real hiring pattern but use sample people data. Evaluate the handoff end to end before discussing broader adoption, identity requirements or integration work.
checks: Run a candidate conversation and panel feedback walkthrough.
Map every onboarding owner, including the handoff to IT.
Document identity, access and integration requirements for production evaluation.
pilot.boundary: Automated account provisioning, production SSO/MFA, live AI and connected external integrations are not claimed in the preview. Global employment and payroll execution remain outside scope.

faqs.q: How is this different from the IT industry page?
faqs.a: This page focuses on companies building technology products and their cross-functional people journey. The IT page addresses technology-services delivery teams; the IT teams solution addresses the internal buyer's responsibilities.

faqs.q: Will it provision accounts for new hires?
faqs.a: No automatic provisioning is demonstrated. Hirebrew can be evaluated for the onboarding responsibility and handoff, while identity, device and application access remain with your IT tools and owners.

faqs.q: Can Brew AI make hiring decisions for us?
faqs.a: No. The website demonstrates illustrative drafts for human review. Selection remains a human decision grounded in agreed criteria, interview evidence and your organisation's approved process.
